<a id="prot_loader_mark"></a>
### [`prot_loader_mark`](../../src/constants.asm#L13) `$0002`

*variable*

Protection: the original loader leaves $32 here and nothing in the program writes it. frame_update wipes memory downward from (row_ptr_top) when it differs; room05_init loops for ever when it differs.

- **Read by:** [`frame_update`](modules/frame_update.md#frame_update) [`$1703`](../../src/frame_update.asm#L256)

<a id="current_player"></a>
### [`current_player`](../../src/constants.asm#L14) `$0003`

*variable*

Player whose turn it is: 0 = player 1 (joystick port 1), 1 = player 2 (port 2). show_title_screen sets 0, lose_fall flips it (EOR 1) in a two-player game. Index of room_unvisited (room*2+player), room13_band_bonus (player*4) and extra_fall_pickups_left.

<a id="contact_col0"></a>
### [`contact_col0`](../../src/constants.asm#L157) `$4EED-$4F03`

*variable*

Background contact tables of check_background_contact, one per mask column (23 bytes each). Index 0-15 = a 4-bit value made of two multicolour pixel codes of a background char under set sprite pixels (high nibble and low nibble of charset byte AND mask). A nonzero entry means the pair was seen. Entries 16-22 hold the pairs 3, 7, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 (pairs with a %11 pixel) seen in chars whose colour RAM colour is not 0; the swap routines move them there. Image residue: $4EED-$4F3D hold a copy of the message bytes $4731-$4781 of an earlier build. At $4F2C the copy reads "DATASO", 6 zero bytes, "SENTS", $A0: the original text "DATASOFT PRESENTS" of message $62 (msg_presents), which this release changed to "DIABOLO  PRESENTS". init_game_variables clears it.

### [`contact_col0_lit`](../../src/constants.asm#L160) `$4F32`

*variable*

1 while the current char of mask column 0/1/2 has a colour RAM colour (bits 0-2) other than 0. While it is 1 the column table is in the swapped state: new %11 hits of coloured chars land in entries 3-15 and the %11 hits of colour-0 chars wait in entries 16-22.

<a id="sprite_buf_a_spr0"></a>
### [`sprite_buf_a_spr0`](../../src/constants.asm#L183) `$8180-$81BF`

*variable*

Sprite blocks $06-$0F (64 bytes each), written at run time; the image bytes do not matter. The sprite builder copy_sprite_frame draws the actors here, buffer A (blocks $06-$0A) and buffer B (blocks $0B-$0F) in turn (sprite_buffer_select selects; sprite_buffer_addresses holds the block addresses, sprite_buffer_pointers the block numbers for sprite_pointers+0..4). Sprite block $06: image of hardware sprite 0 (actor 0 = Bruce, first sprite), buffer A.

<a id="text_font"></a>
### [`text_font`](../../src/constants.asm#L193) `$8800-$88FF`

*variable*

Charset of the title text and the status line (D018 = $32), built by cold_start (copy of the character ROM); the image bytes do not matter. Codes $00-$1F = ROM characters $20-$3F (space, punctuation, digits), $20-$3F = ROM $00-$1F (@, A-Z), $40-$5F and $60-$7F = the same two groups inverted. So code = ASCII - $20 for digits and capitals.

- **Written by:** [`cold_start`](modules/cold_start.md#cold_start) [`$0457`](../../src/cold_start.asm#L83), [`cold_start`](modules/cold_start.md#cold_start) [`$0457`](../../src/cold_start.asm#L83) (+1)

<a id="game_screen"></a>
### [`game_screen`](../../src/constants.asm#L199) `$8C00-$8FF7`

*variable*

Screen RAM ($8C00-$8FE7, 40x25) of the title and the game; the image bytes do not matter to the game. Game layout: row 0 empty, row 1 status line ("1UP 000000 TOP 000000 FALLS 04"), row 2 separator, rows 3-24 the room (11 tile rows of 2 screen rows). $8FE8-$8FF7 are spare; the room decoder writes 2 bytes there for rooms 4, 7, 10, 13, 17, 18. The bytes that the original image had here (an assembler symbol table of the build and an older room charset) are not part of the game; they are kept in leftovers/ (space bank2) and described in docs/leftovers.md.
